questions.0.explain.t: Texts with similar meaning end up close together in vector space.

questions.0.options.0.t: A numeric vector that represents the meaning of a text

questions.0.options.1.t: A special type of prompt that guides the style of the answer

questions.0.options.2.t: The log of a conversation kept for later analysis

questions.0.options.3.t: An API key used to access the model

questions.1.explain.t: Cosine similarity compares the direction of the vectors.

questions.1.options.0.t: With vector distance or similarity, such as cosine

questions.1.options.1.t: By counting how many identical letters the two texts share

questions.1.options.2.t: By comparing the length of the two texts in characters

questions.1.options.3.t: By calculating the SHA-256 hash of each text and comparing them

questions.1.q.t: How do you measure the similarity between two embeddings?

questions.2.explain.t: Query and documents must be vectorized by the same model.

questions.2.options.0.t: The vectors live in different spaces and are not comparable

questions.2.options.1.t: It becomes slower by default, because each query uses two models

questions.2.options.2.t: It increases the network cost by moving larger vectors

questions.2.options.3.t: It prevents the use of chunks of different sizes

questions.2.q.t: Why is mixing different embedding models in the same index a problem?
